## Overview

This collected Braintree article documents the Control Panel Transaction Summary, a high-level, Dashboard-like report of transactions currently categorized as successful or unsuccessful within a selected date range. It supports processing-trend analysis rather than reconciliation.

## Key takeaways

- The report can be run for a selected date range and grouped according to the user's chosen fields.
- In the results table, the selected Group by fields form the rows and transaction statuses form the columns. Displayed amounts represent transactions currently in each status.
- **Do not use current status categorization for reconciliation.** Braintree warns that transaction statuses can change, so the Transaction Summary is a trend-identification tool rather than a reconciliation record.

quotes.text: The Transaction Summary gives you a high-level overview of transactions currently categorized as successful or unsuccessful within a given date range. Think of it as a report version of the Dashboard in your Control Panel.

While the Transaction Summary can be a good tool for identifying processing trends, it should not be used for reconciliation, because transaction statuses can change. [Contact us](/braintree/help/Reconciling) for more guidance.

- Make your selections on how you would like to group your results
- Select your desired date range
- Click the**Run Transaction Summary**button

The Group by fields that you specified when running the summary make up the rows of this table; the columns are [transaction statuses](/braintree/docs/reference/general/statuses#transaction).

The amounts displayed are representative of transactions that are **currently** in these statuses. For example, a transaction that is currently in the Authorized status will show up as part of the total in the Authorized column.
